key_insight: PING embeds advection–diffusion physics in a graph neural network to forecast transport dynamics on irregular sensor networks and improve solar power forecasting.
engineering_relevance: Better intra-day photovoltaic power forecasts can support grid integration by combining satellite cloud observations with ground-based station data.
method: Represent transported particle concentrations as signals on a graph.
Use a discretized advection–diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the training loss.
Couple PING forecasts with photovoltaic power prediction models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on par with state-of-the-art models on synthetic and real transport datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index data, plus improved intra-day PV forecasting.
watch_item: A soft physics constraint does not guarantee physical consistency, and the abstract provides no quantitative PV forecast gains.
paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
